entries.german:

entries.english: I, Konrad von Esserswil, citizen of Arbon, acknowledge that the provost and chapter of the collegiate church of St Stephen in Konstanz had raised disputes against me concerning the Vogtei over the village of Salmsach, which I bought from Egelolf von Rosenberg. The people and property of the village, both serfs and freeholders, belong by hereditary right to the canons and their church. We have settled the dispute amicably as follows. The canons and their officials have the right and power to judge matters concerning their people and property, whether hereditary or held as fiefs, serfs or freeholders. Since jurisdiction and boundaries belong to me by virtue of the Vogtei, I or the future Vogt may judge cases concerning free people; any fines arising from those cases are to be divided equally between the Vogt and the canons. I must exercise the jurisdiction and boundaries belonging to me with due restraint and in a manner for which I can answer to God. I also stated that Egelolf von Rosenberg granted me the Vogtei with the right to succeed him as Vogt over his people. The canons consent to this, provided that I and any successor acknowledge the rents, levies, and services owed to a Vogt, as recorded in their register. I and my successors may also enjoy the fishing rights belonging to a Vogt in the nearby waters, as previous Vogts have done, without prejudice. The church patronage of Salmsach is to be exercised in alternating turns: when it first becomes vacant, the canons shall appoint the incumbent; at the next vacancy, the Vogt shall do so, and the right shall alternate perpetually. Because Egelolf von Rosenberg had captured some of the canons' people, causing me expense and loss in purchasing the Vogtei, the canons graciously grant me and my heirs the next presentation when the church becomes vacant, as compensation. After that appointment, the ordinary alternating sequence resumes: the canons present at the following vacancy, I or my heirs at the next, and so on. The canons reserve that these agreements are not to prejudice any of their rights or those of their church in their other courts, people, or property. In witness and lasting security, I issue this charter for myself, heirs, and successors to the canons and chapter of St Stephen in Konstanz, sealed with my own seal. Given at Konstanz on the Friday before St Matthias the Apostle's Day in 1382. The seal is damaged and measures 2.7 cm.
